doc: Household liquids for the tier-1 physics layer (docs/design/TIER1_PHYSICS.md 4.4; read through props.liquid_props). The physical columns replace food's LIQUID_DENSITY and cleaning's SPILL_PROPS physics; `residue` names the dominant cleaning soil kind a dried spill leaves (cleaning keeps its residue rules). An unknown liquid gets `default`. Aliases map every liquid name used by the type files, the specs and the domain code; an alias may override columns.

columns.visc_cp: dynamic viscosity at room temperature, centipoise (water 1)
columns.freeze_c: freezing point, deg C; null: does not freeze solid in a household freezer
columns.floor_hazard: what a puddle does to a floor: wet, slip or sticky
columns.film_mm: puddle film thickness on a hard floor, mm (puddle area = volume / film)
columns.flammable: true, false or "hot" (only when heated, cooking oil)
columns.toxic: harmful to swallow or touch (people and pets)
columns.perishable: spoils and smells when left (milk, soup)
columns.residue: cleaning soil kind a spill leaves; null: none
columns.clear: colourless and see-through: a puddle of it looks like any clear liquid (water, vinegar, alcohol and bleach are told apart only up close or by the bottle; its glance label says clear liquid)

min_spill_l.source: below 5 ml a spill is droplets: no puddle entity and no harm (unifies navigation SPILL_MIN_L and food SPILL_HARM_G)

water.source: water at 20 C: 998 kg/m3, 1.0 cP; a household puddle spreads to about 1-2 mm

dirty_water.source: mop and rinse water: water with suspended dirt

soapy_water.source: dilute detergent solution: surfactant film makes floors slippery

milk.source: whole milk: 1.03 g/mL, about 2 cP, freezes at -0.54 C; sours where it dries

cream.source: heavy cream: 0.99 g/mL (food LIQUID_DENSITY), fat-rich and slippery

juice.source: fruit juice: about 10-12 % sugar, 1.04-1.05 g/mL; dries sticky

soda.source: sugared soft drink: about 1.04 g/mL; dries sticky

coffee.source: brewed coffee is water-like and stains fabrics and grout

tea.source: brewed tea is water-like; tannin stains like coffee

wine.source: table wine about 12 % alcohol: 0.99 g/mL, freezes about -5 to -7 C; red wine stains

beer.source: beer about 5 % alcohol: 1.01 g/mL, freezes about -2 C

vinegar.source: 5 % acetic acid: 1.01 g/mL, freezes about -2 C

soup.source: cream or puree soup: about 10 cP, salt lowers the freezing point slightly

broth.source: clear stock: water-like with a little fat and salt

oil.source: vegetable cooking oil: 0.92 g/mL (food LIQUID_DENSITY), about 50-80 cP at 20 C; flash point about 300 C (burns only when heated)

motor_oil.source: SAE 10W-30 at 20 C: 0.88 g/mL, about 200-300 cP, pour point about -30 C; hazardous waste

honey.source: honey: 1.42 g/mL, 2,000-10,000 cP at 20 C; does not freeze solid (glass transition)

syrup.source: pancake (corn) syrup: 1.33 g/mL, about 2,500-3,000 cP (pure maple syrup is thinner, about 150 cP)

dish_soap.source: hand dishwashing liquid: 1.03 g/mL, 200-1,000 cP; very slippery underfoot

laundry_detergent.source: liquid laundry detergent: 1.03-1.1 g/mL, a few hundred cP

bleach.source: household bleach (6 % sodium hypochlorite): 1.08-1.10 g/mL, freezes about -7 to -12 C

alcohol.source: ethanol: 0.79 g/mL, 1.1-1.2 cP, flash point 13 C, evaporates fast

gasoline.source: gasoline: 0.71-0.77 g/mL, about 0.6 cP, flash point -43 C

lighter_fluid.source: naphtha charcoal lighter fluid: about 0.70 g/mL, highly flammable

antifreeze.source: 50/50 ethylene glycol coolant: 1.07 g/mL, about 3.5-4 cP, freezes about -37 C; sweet-tasting and poisonous to pets

paint.source: latex wall paint: 1.2-1.4 g/mL, several hundred to 2,000 cP; ruined by freezing

urine.source: urine: 1.005-1.030 g/mL, water-like; a biohazard to clean

vomit.source: vomit: a thick slurry; slippery and a biohazard

raw_egg.source: raw egg: about 1.03 g/mL, viscous white; slippery

mud_water.source: muddy water: suspended soil raises density to about 1.1-1.3 g/mL

isopropyl_alcohol.source: isopropanol: 0.786 g/mL, about 2 cP, flash point 12 C
